catalog_quote: Anii has two surface tone levels, high (H) and low (L), but the L tones are the phonetic pronunciation of toneless syllables, rather than being phonological entities. The tone-bearing unit in Anii is the mora, and the tone patterns reveal that Anii has certain unusual syllable structures. ... Anii has both lexical and grammatical tone. As in many other African languages, there are two categories of verb stem with regard to tonal behavior ... [p.17-18:] As is illustrated in the examples above, Anii has two surface tone levels, high (H), represented by the symbol ˊ and low (L), represented by the symbol ˋ. These tones make lexical meaning distinctions, as shown in (5): (5) a. ùʃìlè ‘sun’ ùʃìlé ‘day’ ... c. dòòdòò ‘far away (in space or time)’ dòodoo ‘be cold’ Besides distinguishing lexical meaning, tone is also part of the grammar of Anii (i.e. tone can have grammatical meaning). ... audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The 'tonal' coding rests on the language's only grammar-length description, a 2014 dissertation whose second half is a dedicated tonology by the principal fieldworker; the deciding quotation is verbatim in the text we hold at the stated locators (abstract ii-iii, Ch.1 pp.17-18), and the negative claim (no Anii stress statement in 479 pp) was re-verified by a full-text search for stress/accent every 'stress/accent/prominence' hit. Glottolog's full 18-item bibliography and Morton's 2025 CV show no competing phonology, JIPA illustration, instrumental study or SIL sketch. Two open handouts downloaded now (ACAL 2013; 2017 workshop slides) restate the analysis and add free LL/LH/HL/HH noun-root patterns, which supports 'tonal' over pitch accent. Nothing found suggests a stress system; no reclassification or re-read needed.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Anii has two tone levels, with both lexical and grammatical tone ... two-syllable noun roots can have LL, LH, HL or HH tone patterns, and the pattern of each word is lexically-defined' (à-ŋɔ̀rɔ̀ 'month', à-sǹ̩á 'dog', à-súko 'horse', gù-fólú 'bamboo'); 'The tone-bearing unit in Anii is the mora. L-toned moras are phonologically toneless.' No stress/accent statement.

sources.quote: 'Gɩsɩda Anii has two phonological tone levels, High (H) and Low (L), and downstep ... exhibits both lexical tone ... and grammatical tone ... L tone is not treated as a phonological entity in itself, but rather as the absence of H tone'; TBU = mora. No mention of stress or accent in Anii.
